title: Home & everyday objects
goal: Describe your home, say where things are, and use 'there is / there are'.
intro:
In this unit you'll learn rooms, furniture and everyday objects, and the postpositions that locate things: **میں** (in), **پر** (on), **کے نیچے** (under), **کے پاس** (near)… Like کا, these come **after** the noun.

You'll also see that 'there is a…' in Urdu is just the verb ہے: 'In the room a bed is' — کمرے میں ایک بستر ہے.

vocab.note: m. گھر ghar = home/house in general.
m. Also باتھ روم; toilet: واش روم.
m. Also پلنگ palang, چارپائی chārpā’ī (rope bed).
m. The ceiling fan is essential in summer.
f. بتی چلی گئی = the power's gone (load-shedding).
f. Flat roofs are used for sleeping in summer and flying kites.
کے پاس = near; also 'have': میرے پاس = I have.
کے ساتھ = with; ساتھ والا کمرہ = the next room

phrases.en: There are three rooms in this house.

grammar.title: Postpositions of place: میں، پر، کے نیچے…
grammar.body:
Urdu uses **postpositions** — they come after the noun. The simple ones are **میں** meṃ 'in', **پر** par 'on, at', **سے** se 'from', **تک** tak 'up to', **کو** ko 'to'.

Others are compounds with **کے**: کے نیچے 'under', کے اوپر 'on top of', کے پاس 'near', کے سامنے 'in front of', کے پیچھے 'behind', کے ساتھ 'with', کے اندر 'inside', کے باہر 'outside', کے درمیان 'between'.

**The oblique case:** a masculine noun ending in -ā changes to -e before any postposition: کمرہ → کمرے میں 'in the room', دروازہ → دروازے کے پیچھے. Plurals take -oṃ: کمروں میں 'in the rooms'. Pronouns change too: یہ → اس is, وہ → اس us: اس کمرے میں 'in this room'.

examples.en: The book is on the table.
The shoes are near the door.
The car is in front of the house.
The children are in the rooms.

grammar.title: 'There is / there are' and 'I have' (میرے پاس)
grammar.body:
'There is/are' is just the verb ہے / ہیں with the place first: **کمرے میں ایک کھڑکی ہے** 'in the room (there) is one window'. The negative: کمرے میں کوئی کھڑکی **نہیں** ہے 'there's no window in the room'.

For owning **things** (not relatives, Unit 3), Urdu says 'near me is': **میرے پاس** گاڑی ہے 'I have a car'. Other forms: آپ کے پاس, اس کے پاس, ہمارے پاس.

Ask with کیا: کیا آپ کے پاس قلم ہے؟ 'Do you have a pen?'

dialogue.title: The new flat
dialogue.setting: Ayesha shows her friend Zainab around her new flat in Karachi.

lines.en: Come, come in! This is my new home.

lines.en: There is — look up! And there's AC in the room too.

lines.speaker: Zainab

lines.en: Still in boxes, behind the cupboard.

culture: Shoes are usually taken off before entering prayer rooms and often before entering homes — watch what your hosts do. Many houses are built around a courtyard (صحن sahn) with a flat roof (چھت) used in summer evenings. Frequent power cuts ('load-shedding', لوڈ شیڈنگ) mean many homes have a UPS or generator, and 'battī chalī ga’ī' is a phrase you'll hear daily.

lessons.title: Rooms of the house

tip.title: 'There is / there are'
tip.body:
- Start with the place, end with **ہے / ہیں**: گھر میں تین کمرے **ہیں** = there are three rooms in the house.
- One thing → **ہے**; more than one → **ہیں**.
- 'There's no …' = **کوئی** … **نہیں** ہے: یہاں کوئی غسل خانہ نہیں ہے.

tip.title: On, in, under: words that come after
tip.body:
- Urdu says 'table **on**': میز **پر** = on the table, کمرے **میں** = in the room.
- Longer ones use **کے**: بستر **کے نیچے** under the bed, میز **کے اوپر** on top of the table.
- Before them, a masculine **-ا / -ہ** word changes to **-ے**: کمرہ → **کمرے** میں.
tip.pattern: thing + place + پر / میں / کے نیچے + ہے

sentences.native: میری چابی بستر کے نیچے ہے۔
sentences.roman: merī chābī bistar ke nīche hai.
sentences.en: My key is under the bed.
The keys aren't on the table.
What's on top of the table?

sentences.native: اس کمرے میں صرف ایک کرسی ہے۔

sentences.en: There's only one chair in this room.

sentences.native: میری کتابیں سونے کے کمرے میں ہیں۔
sentences.roman: merī kitābeṃ sone ke kamre meṃ haiṃ.
sentences.en: My books are in the bedroom.

tip.title: Inside, outside: کے اندر, کے باہر
tip.body:
- **اندر** inside, **باہر** outside. With a place, add **کے**: گھر **کے باہر** = outside the house.
- The -ا/-ہ word before them changes: دروازہ → **دروازے** کے باہر.
- **تشریف رکھیے** is the very polite 'please sit down' — say it to any guest.

sentences.en: Come in, please have a seat.
The kids are outside the door.
The key is inside the cupboard.

sentences.native: اس کمرے میں کوئی کھڑکی نہیں ہے۔
sentences.roman: is kamre meṃ ko’ī khiṛkī nahīṃ hai.
sentences.en: There's no window in this room.
There's a lot of water on the floor.

tip.title: Asking someone to switch it on
tip.body:
- **چلا دیں** = please switch on, **بند کر دیں** = please switch off (polite).
- To a friend or child: **چلا دو, بند کر دو**.
- **بتی چلی گئی** — 'the light has gone' — is what everyone says when the power cuts out.

sentences.en: There's no fan in the room.
The dishes are in the kitchen.

sentences.native: اوپر آ جائیں، کھانا لگ گیا ہے۔
sentences.roman: ūpar ā jā’eṃ, khānā lag gayā hai.
sentences.en: Come on up, the food's ready.
The car is behind the house.

sentences.native: میرا گھر آپ کے گھر کے سامنے ہے۔
sentences.roman: merā ghar āp ke ghar ke sāmne hai.

sentences.native: میز دو کرسیوں کے درمیان ہے۔
sentences.roman: mez do kursiyoṃ ke darmiyān hai.
sentences.en: The table is between two chairs.

sentences.native: غسل خانہ سونے کے کمرے کے ساتھ ہے۔
sentences.roman: ġusl xāna sone ke kamre ke sāth hai.
sentences.en: The bathroom is next to the bedroom.

lessons.title: What I have

tip.title: I have: میرے پاس
tip.body:
- For things you own, Urdu says 'near me is': **میرے پاس** گاڑی ہے = I have a car.
- Others: **آپ کے پاس, ہمارے پاس, تمہارے پاس, اس کے پاس**.
- Ask with کیا: کیا آپ کے پاس چابی ہے؟ (For family, use میرا / میری instead.)
tip.pattern: میرے پاس + thing + ہے / نہیں ہے
